candidates.rationale: Drupal nav is logo + flat ul.menu with two nested submenus (Policyholders, Agents/Brokers) + a mobile .menu-icon. The boilerplate header covers every one of those: it marks any li containing a nested ul as .nav-drop, and injects its own hamburger below 900px.
Identical to the internal copy; no reason to re-vendor.
Could lay out nav items, but carries no nav semantics, keyboard handling or mobile toggle.

migration_note: IMPLEMENTED as a hard-coded block (blocks/header/header.js). Content is NOT authored in AEM yet, so the nav lives in a NAV_ITEMS array in the block rather than in a /nav fragment document; buildNav() emits the same DOM loadFragment() would have, so switching to fragment-driven content later is a one-function change. Covers all 6 top-level items and both 5-company submenus, with aria-current set from the URL. Logo extracted from the source site to icons/logo.webp. The Drupal data-drupal-link-system-path and is-active attributes are dropped.

decomposition.reason: Per-page image, no text over it.
Byte-identical on all 20 pages apart from its heading label; belongs in one fragment document, not 20 copies.

candidates.rationale: Shares the 'full-width banner image at top of page' intent, but the contracts diverge: hero absolutely positions the picture behind an overlaid h1, while every one of the 20 captured banners is image-only with a text sidebar beside it.
gaps: image-only variant - hero.css styles h1 over the image and there is no heading in any captured banner
side-by-side layout - source is a 3-col sidebar + 9-col image, hero is single-column full-bleed
hero model requires a text richtext field that would sit empty on all 20 pages

candidates.rationale: Structurally the closer match to the raw markup - a 2-cell row that is text on the left and a picture on the right, which is exactly what columns renders and it already tags the image cell .columns-img-col.
gaps: still bakes the repeated sidebar into every page

candidates.rationale: Scored against the sidebar half only. The sidebar is site-wide chrome and fragment is the boilerplate's designed answer for content repeated across pages.

migration_note: The 0.6 detector confidence was warranted - this is not one component. Recommended split: (a) the banner image becomes hero with an image-only variant, adding a CSS rule that drops the absolute positioning when the block has no heading, and making the model's text field optional; (b) the sidebar becomes a single /fragment/login-links document referenced once per page, or lifted into the section template. Two label variants exist across the 20 pages - 'Please choose your login:' and 'Quick links:' - both wrapping the same two links (/policyholders, /agentbrokers), so the fragment needs one heading variant, not twenty copies. Crop check (home/cmp-002.png) confirms no text sits over the image and that the two sidebar links render as solid buttons - author them as standalone links in their own paragraphs so the boilerplate button decoration picks them up, rather than porting the Drupal button CSS.

candidates.rationale: Source footer is two paragraphs - a pipe-separated link pair (Disclosures | Privacy Policy) and a copyright line. The boilerplate footer passes fragment content through untouched, which is exactly what this needs.

migration_note: IMPLEMENTED as a hard-coded block (blocks/footer/footer.js). Content is NOT authored in AEM yet, so the links and copyright live in the block rather than in a /footer fragment document; buildFooter() is a one-function swap when content lands. The link pair is rendered as a list with CSS-drawn dividers rather than literal '|' characters, and the external Privacy Policy link carries rel=noopener noreferrer. OPEN QUESTION: the copyright still reads 2014 as in the source - confirm the intended year with the client before publishing.
